Hazard Ratios from Cox Proportional Hazards Models

Source: R/estimate_hazard_ratio.R
estimate_hazard_ratio.Rd

Fits Cox proportional hazards models (survival::coxph()) with the treatment arm as the explanatory variable, and reports the hazard ratio of each arm against the control arm (the first level of ARM). The unadjusted model is always fitted; models adjusted for covariates, stratified by strata, or both are added when these are given.

Usage

estimate_hazard_ratio(
  data,
  covariates = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  ties = c("efron", "breslow", "exact"),
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by processing_dataset, with two or more treatment arms.

covariates

Character vector with the names of covariate columns of data for the adjusted models. The default is NULL.

strata

Character vector with the names of stratification columns of data for the stratified models. The default is NULL.

ties

Method for tied event times: "efron" (the default of survival::coxph()), "breslow" or "exact".

conf_level

Confidence level, a single number in (0, 1). The default is 0.95.

Value

A data frame with one row per model and comparison, and the columns model ("Unadjusted, unstratified", "Unadjusted, stratified", "Adjusted, unstratified" or "Adjusted, stratified"), covariates and strata (the columns used, "None" if none), comparison (for example "Treatment vs Control"), hr, lcl, ucl (Wald confidence interval), p_value (Wald test), n and events (observations and events used by the model).

Examples

raw <- generate_dummy_survival_data(
  arm = c("Control", "Treatment"), n = c(100, 100),
  hazards = log(2) / c(12, 18), dropout_per_year = 0.1, seed = 123
)
dat <- processing_dataset(raw, column_arm = "ARM",
                          column_survtime = "SURVTIME",
                          column_cnsr = "CNSR", control_arm = "Control")
estimate_hazard_ratio(dat)
#>                      model covariates strata           comparison        hr
#> 1 Unadjusted, unstratified       None   None Treatment vs Control 0.6842886
#>        lcl       ucl    p_value   n events
#> 1 0.501417 0.9338553 0.01678775 200    167
